notes: kind 'finding' = required; 'fp_guard' = must not be reported; 'tolerated' = neither required nor penalized (text supports both readings). accepted_alternatives lists equivalent pattern_id spellings that must score as the same label.

decisions.dispute: #4k at tests/beacon-readings.spec.ts:4 - author P0 (instance escalation) vs both blind P1
decisions.verdict: change to P1; drop author's P1 fp_guard; P0 not accepted
decisions.quote: references/reporting.md:134 'A pattern's severity is its usual case; an instance can be reported higher when it meets the P0 definition outright, the way `#12` already conditions P0 on the wrong surface actually satisfying the test's assertions.' | references/patterns/4.md:39 '#4b-#4e and #4g-#4k are P1: they can fail, but provide weak, non-retrying, or under-specified evidence ...' | references/patterns/4.md:191 'FLAG P1 - the loop body holds the only assertions and nothing constrains the collection size.'
decisions.reason: The #4k contract assigns P1 to exactly this shape (only assertions in the loop, no count proof), and 'outright' escalation needs evidence that the broken state actually satisfies the assertions (the #12 analogue); here rendered rows would still be checked for 'Healthy', and nothing in the case shows the collection is empty, so the test can fail and P0 is not met outright.

decisions.dispute: #4i at cypress/e2e/map-archive.cy.ts:5 - author P0 (instance escalation) vs both blind P1
decisions.verdict: change to P1; drop author's P1 fp_guard; P0 not accepted
decisions.quote: references/patterns/4.md:93 '4i. Absence assertion never proven able to match ... [P1]' | references/patterns/4.md:119 'FLAG P1 - the locator appears nowhere else on that test's execution path ... and nothing positive is asserted alongside.' | references/reporting.md:134 (escalation only 'when it meets the P0 definition outright').
decisions.reason: The case matches the #4i FLAG P1 condition word for word, and nothing supplied (no source or fixture) shows the ribbon selector matches nothing, so the silent pass is possible but not proven; the text therefore does not support P0 outright.

decisions.dispute: #4f at tests/kiln.spec.ts:13 - Codex composite '#4f + #6'; Claude adds #1 P0 at line 2
decisions.verdict: keep author #4f P0 and accept '#4f + #6' as the same label; keep #6 fp_guard; #1 at line 2 tolerated (not required, not penalized)
decisions.quote: references/semantic-review.md:89 'If a single code block triggers multiple checks ... report it as ONE finding with all rule numbers in the heading (e.g., `[P0] #4f + #6: ...`).' | references/patterns/1.md:28 'Anchor #1 to the test/setup declaration whose title contains the unverified promise. A constant or unrelated assertion that fails to prove the noun is supporting evidence, not a second #1 finding.' | references/semantic-review.md:93 'Report the single causal line ... An adjacent explanatory or assertion line is evidence, not a second finding.'
decisions.reason: Codex's '#4f + #6' is the exact heading form the consolidation rule prescribes, so it should score as the #4f P0 label. For #1, patterns/1.md:28 reads a constant assertion as evidence for a #1 finding at the title. The single-causal-line contract, though, supports reporting the invariant assertion as the one finding. No text picks between the two, so #1 at the title is tolerated rather than required. Line 11 has the same shape (its only assertion is the invariant #4f), so the same treatment applies there.

decisions.verdict: keep author #4f P0 and accept '#4f + #6' as the same label; keep #6 fp_guard; #1 at line 2 tolerated for consistency
decisions.quote: references/semantic-review.md:89 'report it as ONE finding with all rule numbers in the heading (e.g., `[P0] #4f + #6: ...`)'; references/reporting.md:94 'When one block reports several patterns, list every ID, such as `#9 #10a`.'
decisions.reason: The composite ID is the prescribed consolidated heading, not a separate finding, so it must match the author's #4f P0; only a separate #6 P1 row is excluded.

decisions.dispute: Claude adds #1 P0 at cypress/e2e/compost.cy.ts:2; author has #1 fp_guard there
decisions.verdict: drop author's #1 fp_guard; #1 at line 2 tolerated (not required, not penalized)
decisions.quote: references/patterns/1.md:26 'P0 when no promised outcome in the title has evidence' | references/patterns/1.md:28 'A constant or unrelated assertion that fails to prove the noun is supporting evidence, not a second #1 finding.' | references/semantic-review.md:89 consolidation applies to 'the same lines of code'.
decisions.reason: The fp_guard's premise, that consolidation absorbs #1 into #4a, is not in the text: consolidation covers the same lines, and patterns/1.md:28 treats a constant assertion as evidence for #1 at the title. The only #1 exclusions in the text are for #2, #20/#22 and #23, never #4a. The single-causal-line contract still makes #4a alone a valid report, so #1 is tolerated rather than required.

decisions.dispute: Claude adds #4i P1 at tests/bloom.spec.ts:7; author has #4i fp_guard there
decisions.verdict: drop author's #4i fp_guard; #4i P1 at line 7 tolerated (accepted alternative, not required)
decisions.quote: references/patterns/4.md:117 'SKIP - the test is an empty-state / no-results case that also asserts a positive counterpart ... It does not cover the `#23` case: when a render guard suppresses seeded items ... the positive counterpart proves nothing.' | references/patterns/4.md:119 'FLAG P1 - the locator appears nowhere else on that test's execution path ... and nothing positive is asserted alongside.' | references/patterns/23.md:14 'The negative assertion or missing-element failure it causes is supporting evidence, not the causal line.'
decisions.reason: The #4i FLAG conditions are met literally, and 4.md:117 explicitly says #4i's skip does not rescue a #23 case, so flagging #4i there cannot be a false positive. On the other side, 23.md:14 and semantic-review.md:93 support treating the assertion as #23 evidence only, so neither reading is mandatory.

decisions.dispute: Codex adds #4a P0 for expect(2 + 2).toBe(4) at tests/aurora.spec.ts:6
decisions.verdict: add finding #4a P0 at line 6 (author's #15 fp_guard at the same line stays)
decisions.quote: references/patterns/4.md:4 'An assertion is logically unable to fail' | references/patterns/4.md:39 '#4a and #4f are P0 because their predicates are true independently of product behavior.'
decisions.reason: 2 + 2 === 4 is a literal invariant independent of the product, the same class the author labels #4a P0 in v17-pw-05:5 (literal 1200) and v17-cy-15:5 (Math.abs(-5)); omitting it here is inconsistent with the contract.

decisions.dispute: Claude adds #22 P1 at tests/tag-forge.spec.ts:5 besides author's #20
decisions.quote: references/patterns/22.md:21 'Flag P1 only when the test or supplied acceptance contract promises a backend call or persisted result, repository evidence proves the asserted UI state is optimistic, and no assertion proves the promised backend effect. ... a test scoped to client-visible UI state may intentionally prove only that state' | references/patterns/22.md:23 'Do not infer a backend contract or optimistic behavior from a write-shaped action name alone.'
decisions.reason: The optimistic 'Tag queued' state is proven from source, but neither the title 'forges a lunar tag' nor any acceptance contract promises a backend call or persisted result; the comment only describes the CI environment, which is #20's evidence, so #22's first precondition fails.

decisions.verdict: accept alternative: #10f P1 at line 4 tolerated (not required, not penalized)
decisions.quote: references/patterns/10.md:55 '10f ... an action such as `.click()` or `.type()` is followed by another assertion/action in the same chain ... Skip when project evidence proves the subject remains stable and the chain is intentionally atomic.' | references/semantic-review.md:50 'Bounded opening-token sweep (MANDATORY, exactly this list - no more, no less)' with semantic-review.md:73 '#10f | Cypress actions beyond the scanner's list: ... `.clear` ... followed by `.should(` on the same chain'.
decisions.reason: The definition covers any action followed by another action, and .clear() is named as an action, so Codex's hit fits the contract. The mandated sweep, however, only reaches .clear when .should( follows, and the scanner (actions click/type/check/... followed by more chain) does not fire here, so a reviewer following the procedure would not find it. Both readings are text-supported.

decisions.dispute: author #4k P1 at cypress/e2e/bell-tower.cy.ts:4; neither blind labeler reports it
decisions.verdict: drop author finding; convert to fp_guard #4k P1 at line 4
decisions.quote: references/patterns/4.md:179 '`cy.get()`, `.find()`, and `.filter()` are retryable DOM queries with implicit existence checks; appending `.each()` does not remove those checks. Do not report ... as silent empty iteration merely because the selector might match nothing.' | references/patterns/4.md:188 'SKIP - Cypress DOM queries retain an implicit existence check on the iterated subject; a missing expected count is not by itself proof of silent empty iteration.'
decisions.reason: cy.get('[data-cy=bell]') fails when nothing matches, so the .each() loop cannot silently run zero times; the #4k contract explicitly skips this shape, which contradicts the author's finding (and the author's design note).

undisputed_flags.issue: Design-note intent (test the reporting.md escalation clause) cannot be met by these sources as written.
undisputed_flags.reason: To justify an 'outright' P0 instance, the case would need supplied evidence that the broken state actually satisfies the assertion (e.g., source proving the ribbon selector never renders or the reading list is empty), the same standard reporting.md:134 cites for #12.
